subject: info-doc
title: (R)INFO.DOC. ------CULT.SOLD.
description: Diagram in CMOA(II)-9 (Creative Music Outside of America, Level One — France/Italy/Northern Europe/Japan) opening Braxton's France analysis: 'black creativity has long enjoyed the support of the French public on many different levels … most people in France have some level of awareness about creative black music—which is not to say that every given person must necessarily like every aspect.' (R)INFO-DOC (the reality of information documentation) is crossed with CULT-SOLD (culture solidification): the question is what information-documentation produces in its actual instantiation when crossed with culture-solidification — the (R) prefix marking that real documentation (French television, radio, concert schedules) is what makes the crossing productive. The main line ends at (P)CULT-SOLD (culture solidification at its point of idea completion) on the upper right. PROG-CONT (progressional continuance) branches from the main line and carries two branches. On one, (R)INT (the reality of intention) drops below; AF-DY (affinity dynamics) branches from it to the left margin, and P-FC (particular focus) branches from AF-DY. On the other, PHY-U-P (physical universe particular) runs to the upper right; STF (source transfer) branches from it, MT-INFO (multi-information) and TRS (transition) branch from STF, and GRAD (gradualism) branches from TRS. Structural argument: information-documentation-as-real crossed with culture-solidification has progressional-continuance as central hub. The diagram exposes Braxton's structural diagnostic of why France produces a healthy creative-music infrastructure: real documentation (broadcasters, concert venues) actually obtains and the progressional-continuance hub holds.
